citations.narrative:
There was no written Program of Veterinary Care (PVC) available for review from the new Attending Veterinarian. The
facility recently switched to a new Attending Veterinarian but did not have a signed PVC from them. A written PVC
outlines instructions given by the Attending Veterinarian to the facility for how to care for the regulated animals including
physical examinations, vaccinations, fecal sampling, heartworm sampling, de-worming and preventative care. Lack of a
signed program of veterinary care from the Attending Veterinarian can lead to insufficient routine veterinary care, and
untimely diagnosis and treatment of the animals. Each dealer must follow an appropriate program of veterinary care for
dogs that is developed, documented in writing, and signed by the current Attending Veterinarian. Facilities must keep and
maintain the written document and make it available for APHIS inspection. Correct by having the current Attending
Veterinarian sign a PVC that fulfills all requirements. Correct by 22-OCT-2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the Licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
